title: The 2026 Midterms Just Exposed AI's Biggest Problem
description:
The 2026 midterms showed that AI has a big marketing problem. 56% of voters called it a crucial or major factor. Voters also went against data centers in 40 of 41 local ballot measures.

I've been rather neutral on AI on this channel, and I've acknowledged the utility plenty of times. But a lot of people are so focused on what this technology can do that they miss how regular people feel about it, and being right on the facts won't fix that for you. So I went through the polling, the money and the politics of what just happened.

In this video:
- Why usage keeps going up while public sentiment gets more negative
- Jobs, power bills and the data center backlash
- How the people running these companies and the pro-AI crowd made it worse
- What AI has done to gamers, game stores and indie developers
- The money: spending, losses and who covers the difference
- How the parties flipped on AI, and what the exit polls said
- What this could mean for the people who want this technology to win

title: Until you fix this...
description:
Why culture matters more than politics, and why nothing changes until it does. Hollywood wasn't always one-sided. Here's how it changed hands, what the numbers look like now, and what it takes to build again.

I've been in two Billboard-charting bands and built the Rippaverse into a company that's done over sixteen million dollars in sales. At that level, I can count the people on my side of the aisle on one hand. That's not a complaint. It's a data point.

In this one I go through the history: the 1944 Motion Picture Alliance, Walt Disney and Ronald Reagan in front of Congress in 1947, the Paramount decision, the film-school generation and the long march through the institutions. Then the receipts: the donation numbers, why right of center audiences are more tolerant and why that works against them, why artists in the mainstream stay quiet, and why a studio like BioWare closing isn't a victory.

This isn't a political video. It's about a return to normal: creators create freely, people disagree on politics and still enjoy the same things, and nobody gets cancelled or shunned. You don't take back a table you never valued. You build your own.

title: It'll never return...
description:
90s nostalgia hits different, and it isn't just because we got older. We were the last generation to grow up before the internet took over everything: an analog childhood, then the world changed underneath us.

Psychologists call it the reminiscence bump: you remember ages 10 to 30 more vividly than any other part of your life. Everybody has one. What's different is what was happening during ours. In this video I break down the five reasons: everything was scarce, there was real mystery, we all watched the same things at the same time, we owned physical things, and we're the bridge generation that saw the world before and after.

title: You're Not Paying What AI Actually Costs
description:
AI pricing doesn't match what AI costs to run. Your monthly fee is flat, but every prompt costs the company real computing power, and the gap is being covered by investors.

Over the weekend Elon Musk said the cost of serving Grok Bot was "unsustainably high relative to revenue," two weeks after calling it the fastest-growing product he'd ever seen. That isn't just an xAI problem. In this video I break down how flat-rate AI plans actually work, why AI agents broke the buffet model, how few people pay at all, who is covering the losses, and the quiet changes already happening: weekly caps, lighter default models, shared usage pools and token meters.

If you've built your workflow, your business or your content around these tools, plan for a correction. Today's price is not the real price.
